answer: A sybil shield that works is pay-per-packet admission. Each agent buys a violet chip priced in verifiable compute: one chip admits one session, every puppet buys its own, so cost grows linearly with N and there is no bulk discount. The registrar's cryptographic quill signs a chip only after a fresh proof of real CPU work, so forging costs more than honesty. Honest users pay once and reclaim the toll on exit; a sybil operator in a sable identity must repay the same price per puppet, so flooding drains its budget faster than fake votes earn.
